creators.name: Maya
creators.bio: I grew up here and came back after two years in Portland. I work the front desk at a dental office and film on my lunch break. My first video was about the three apartments in town I could look at and the one I could afford.
creators.caption: Three apartments in town. One I could afford. Here is what the lease said.
creators.scene: A one-bedroom apartment lease on a kitchen table in morning light, a pen, a mug, a hand turning the page

creators.name: Devin
creators.bio: I wanted to sell coffee from a cart outside the hospital. It took eleven signatures and most of a winter. I make videos about what each form was for, in the order I had to get them.
creators.caption: I wanted to sell coffee from a cart. It took eleven signatures.
creators.scene: A small coffee cart on a snowy sidewalk at dawn, steam rising from a cup, a stack of forms clipped to a board

creators.name: Priya
creators.bio: Half of my graduating class left Maine. I stayed and started asking the others why. I film the conversations on the mill walk by the river, one person at a time.
creators.caption: Half my graduating class left. I asked the ones who stayed why.
creators.scene: A brick mill building by a river at golden hour, a footpath along the water, two empty chairs facing each other

creators.name: Cole
creators.bio: Forty minutes each way to a job that pays the rent, barely. I mount the phone on the dash and talk through the math while I drive. The numbers are real and so is the gas.
creators.caption: Forty minutes each way for a job that pays the rent. Barely.
creators.scene: A two-lane coastal road at six in the morning seen through a windshield, fog over spruce trees, the dashboard clock reading 6:04

creators.name: Jess
creators.bio: I moved back in with my parents at 26. I have a degree and a full-time job and a spreadsheet that explains the rest. My videos walk through one row of it at a time.
creators.caption: I moved back in with my parents at 26. Here is the math that made me.
creators.scene: A childhood bedroom with a laptop open to a budget spreadsheet on a small desk, a packed duffel bag on the floor, late afternoon window light

creators.name: Tyler
creators.bio: First lease, first security deposit, first surprise fee. I am 21 and learning the rules by hitting them. I keep every receipt and read them out loud on camera.
creators.caption: My first lease. My first security deposit. My first surprise fee.
creators.scene: A set of apartment keys and a stack of receipts on an empty apartment floor, a cardboard box, bare walls, window light

creators.name: Amara
creators.bio: One job pays for the room. The second one pays for everything else. I film between shifts, usually in the car, and I keep it to the parts people never say out loud.
creators.caption: One job pays for the room. The second one pays for everything else.
creators.scene: Two work aprons hanging on hooks by a door, a name tag on each, a wall clock, evening light on a harbor town street outside the window

creators.name: Noah
creators.bio: I am finishing a nursing license and adding up what it costs before the first paycheck: exams, fees, background checks, gas to Presque Isle. I show the receipts, not the speech.
creators.caption: What a nursing license costs before the first paycheck.
creators.scene: Nursing textbooks, a calculator and a stack of fee receipts on a desk under a lamp, snow falling past a dark window

creators.name: Sam
creators.bio: Landscaping stops in November. I film what I do until April: plowing, odd jobs, the weeks with nothing. The off season is the part nobody budgets for, so I do it on camera.
creators.caption: Landscaping stops in November. What I do until April.
creators.scene: A pickup truck with a plow blade in a snowy driveway at dusk, a rake and a shovel leaning on a garage wall
